practice_description.medium: Installation, video, machine learning, hand-labeled datasets, drawing, photography
practice_description.practice_summary: Artist who treats datasets as artistic medium, hand-labeling thousands of training images as a form of craft practice. Her work foregrounds the labor, subjectivity, and provenance of training data, making visible the human decisions embedded in machine learning systems.
practice_description.methodology: Ridler creates her own training datasets from scratch -- photographing, categorizing, and hand-labeling thousands of images (e.g., 10,000 tulip photographs for Myriad/Mosaic Virus). She trains GANs on these bespoke datasets, treating the entire pipeline from data collection to model training to output generation as creative acts. The labor of dataset creation is foregrounded as craft, drawing parallels to historical practices like botanical illustration and tulip mania speculation. She studied at the Royal College of Art and has a background in literature, bringing narrative and historical framing to technical processes.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Ridler's practice demonstrates how data provenance and dataset creation can function as primary artistic material. Her hand-labeled datasets are artworks in themselves, modeling how human-curated knowledge structures could serve as substrate in a graph-curated generative exhibition.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes -- her datasets (e.g., the 10,000 hand-labeled tulip photographs) function as substrate layers that generate downstream artworks. The dataset is simultaneously documentation, craft object, and generative source material. Multiple works emerge from the same dataset.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Partial -- Mosaic Virus links tulip image generation to Bitcoin price data, creating a relational composition between financial markets and botanical imagery. The relationship between individual labeled images and emergent GAN outputs is itself a compositional logic.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partial -- Mosaic Virus changes in response to live Bitcoin price fluctuations, with the 'health' of generated tulips reflecting market conditions. However, the underlying dataset is fixed rather than continuously evolving.

works.title: Myriad (Tulips)
works.description: Installation displaying all 10,000 hand-photographed and individually labeled tulip images used to train a GAN. Each image is categorized by Ridler according to color, shape, and stripe pattern. The dataset itself is presented as the artwork.
works.relevance: Foundational example of dataset-as-artwork. Makes visible the subjective human labor inside machine learning. Directly models how hand-curated knowledge can function as primary artistic material.

works.title: Mosaic Virus
works.description: Three-screen video installation of GAN-generated tulips whose visual characteristics (stripe patterns, 'infection' level) are driven by real-time Bitcoin price data. References 17th-century Dutch tulip mania and the Tulip Breaking Virus.
works.relevance: Demonstrates relational/responsive composition -- artwork determined by external data input. The connection between financial speculation and botanical beauty is a graph-like conceptual link made generative.

works.title: The Shell Record
works.description: Work using hand-collected and labeled shell specimens to explore classification systems, taxonomy, and the relationship between natural variation and machine categorization.
works.relevance: Extends the dataset-as-medium approach to natural history and taxonomy, showing how classification systems themselves are creative and subjective acts -- directly relevant to how a knowledge graph curates and categorizes.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Ridler's practice treats the data pipeline itself as artistic protocol: the rules for how images are photographed, the taxonomy for labeling, and the training parameters all constitute creative decisions that shape output. She designs classification systems and labeling protocols as creative acts, though she does not build governance infrastructure in the way that DAO-based artists do.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Bespoke dataset creation and labeling taxonomies -- custom classification systems for tulips (by stripe pattern, color, shape) and shells that determine how GANs learn to generate images. These taxonomies are artistic protocols that produce visual output.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Ridler's datasets are created entirely by her own labor rather than scraped, giving them clear provenance. She has been vocal about data ethics and the importance of understanding what is inside training datasets. Her work functions as advocacy for transparency in ML data practices, though her datasets and models are not typically released as open-source commons resources.

governance_model.governance_detail: Ridler operates as a solo artist making all creative and technical decisions about dataset creation, labeling taxonomy, model training, and presentation. There is no collective or algorithmic governance layer, though her work implicitly raises questions about who should govern classification systems.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Consent is embedded by design -- Ridler photographs and labels all training data herself, eliminating the ethical problems of scraped or non-consented datasets. Every image in her datasets is self-generated, making provenance and consent unambiguous.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo with machine co-authorship. Ridler is the sole human author who creates datasets and designs training protocols. The GAN is treated as a collaborator that introduces unpredictable variation, but creative authority remains with Ridler through her control of input data and training parameters.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Mosaic Virus responds to live Bitcoin price data, with tulip imagery changing in real time based on market fluctuations. Other works like Myriad are static installations of fixed datasets. The GAN outputs are generative but produced from fixed training sets rather than continuously evolving data.

data_materiality.data_sources: Self-photographed botanical specimens (10,000+ tulip photographs, shell collections), hand-drawn labels and taxonomies, live financial data (Bitcoin prices for Mosaic Virus).
data_materiality.data_provenance: Fully self-generated and consented. All image datasets are photographed and labeled by Ridler herself. Financial data is from public market feeds. No scraped, borrowed, or non-consented data. The provenance chain is a central theme of the work.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Ridler's GAN-based works operate in latent spaces where the model learns to encode and generate images based on her hand-labeled datasets. She navigates the latent space to find outputs, and the relationship between label categories and latent dimensions is a key creative concern. Her work makes the latent space tangible by connecting it to physical, hand-labeled source material.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Primarily visual (photography, video, installation) with conceptual links to financial data and textual classification systems. Not multimodal in a unified embedding sense.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Myriad is displayed as a large-scale grid of 10,000 printed photographs covering gallery walls, creating an immersive field of labeled images. Mosaic Virus uses multi-screen video projection. Works are typically shown in gallery settings that emphasize the scale of the dataset and the labor involved in its creation.

interoperability.composability: Moderate -- datasets could theoretically be used as training data for other models or as structured input for other generative systems, but they are not published as open resources with APIs or standard formats.
interoperability.technical_openness: Partially documented. Ridler presents and discusses her methodology extensively in talks and writing. The datasets and trained models themselves are not typically released as open-source.

technical_approach.stack: GANs (StyleGAN, pix2pix), Python, TensorFlow/PyTorch, custom photography and labeling workflows, real-time data feeds (financial APIs for Mosaic Virus), multi-channel video display systems.

network_position.scene_affiliation: AI art and machine learning art community (central figure); London digital art scene; Royal College of Art alumni; Ars Electronica; Barbican; V&A; Serpentine; PHI Foundation Montreal; international biennials and media art festivals.
network_position.connections: Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst (shared AI art discourse); Refik Anadol (GAN-based art, different approach); Mario Klingemann (GAN art); Memo Akten (AI art); Jake Elwes (GAN art); Nora Al-Badri; connected to broader AI ethics discourse through Spawning AI/Have I Been Trained conversations.

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Ridler's practice is a reference case for data provenance as creative practice -- directly relevant to A(DAI)'s emphasis on transparent, ethical data pipelines. Her hand-labeling methodology models how human curatorial judgment structures machine intelligence. Could serve as a conversation partner on dataset ethics, or as a theoretical reference for how classification systems shape knowledge graphs.
